items.title: [Feature]: IndexCache support for DeepSeek V4
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

Extend the existing IndexCache feature (currently only supported for DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 DSA models) to DeepSeek V4's c4a attention layers, which also use DSA lightning indexer with top-k token selection.

### Motivation

DeepSeek V4 uses a hybrid compressed attention architecture with two layer types:

- **c4a layers** (30 layers): Compressed KV + **DSA lightning indexer** (top-k=1024) + sparse attention
- **c128a layers** (31 layers): Heavily compressed KV, near-full attention (no indexer needed)
- **SWA layer** (1 layer): Pure sliding window, no indexer

The 30 c4a layers have the same DSA lightning indexer as V3.2, making them **directly amenable to IndexCache optimization** — skipping redundant top-k computation across layers by reusing cached `topk_indices`.

This is not theoretical — **vllm-ascend has already implemented and validated it**:

items.title: [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

items.title: Fix GLM tool results with auto chat template content format
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
- special-case GLM-style chat templates during `auto` content-format detection
- keep these templates on the `string` path when they require raw string tool responses
- add renderer regressions for format detection and prompt rendering of tool results

Fixes #39614.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR
- I checked open PRs that reference `#39614` and did not find another open PR for this issue.
- I also checked nearby GLM-related PRs; the open PR `#39253` is about GLM tool parser streaming and does not address prompt rendering of tool result content.

## Root cause
`resolve_chat_template_content_format(..., given_format="auto", ...)` classified certain GLM templates as `openai` because they iterate over `message.content` for regular messages. That causes tool-role messages to be converted into OpenAI-style structured content items before rendering. For GLM templates that explicitly expect `m.content is string` for tool responses, the rendered prompt then falls into the wrong branch and emits an empty `<tools>` wrapper instead of the actual tool result text.

## Tests run
- `python -m py_compile vllm/renderers/hf.py tests/renderers/test_hf.py` ✅
- `python -m pytest --noconftest tests/renderers/test_hf.py -k "glm_tool_response_template" -q` ❌
  - blocked by local environment mismatch during import: the machine's installed `torch` is older than current vLLM expects (`torch.library.infer_schema` is missing)

## AI assistance
This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I reviewed the changed files, commit, and PR description before submission.

## Purpose

`Glm4MoeMTP` is not decorated with `@support_torch_compile`. As a result, the MTP draft forward executes as eager Python and misses every Inductor fusion pass that the target forward enjoys - most notably the AITER allreduce + RMSNorm fusion, RMSNorm + quant fusion, and silu+mul+fp8-quant fusion.

Adding the decorator brings MTP behaviour in line with the canonical `DeepSeekMTP` pattern (`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py`, L185) and makes the draft eligible for the same compile-time fusions as the target.

## Changes

Single-file, two-line wiring in `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_mtp.py`, mirroring `deepseek_mtp.py`:

- Add `from vllm.compilation.decorators import support_torch_compile`.
- Decorate the top-level `Glm4MoeMTP` class with `@support_torch_compile`.

No changes to the forward signature, the loader, or `Glm4MoeMultiTokenPredictor`. `dynamic_arg_dims` is inferred from the existing `forward` annotations (the four `Tensor | None` / `IntermediateTensors | None` args become dim-0 dynamic), exactly as for `DeepSeekMTP`.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: store draft KV cache in model dtype for MLA-only cache layouts; fail fast on DCP
items.bodyExcerpt:
FIX #48380

Two DSpark fixes for DSA-family targets:

1. **Draft cache dtype.** With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` the DSpark draft — a dense (non-MLA) Qwen3-style transformer — inherited the target's `cache_config` and tried to use the MLA-only fp8_ds_mla layout, which no dense attention backend accepts (`ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda ...`). `load_dspark_model` now falls back to the model dtype for the draft's KV cache; the draft cache is a few dense layers, so the memory cost is negligible.
2. **DCP fail-fast.** The DFlash/DSpark draft slot mapping is DCP-blind (`ctx_pos // block_size`), so with `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` the draft reads wrong KV blocks and acceptance silently collapses to ~0% (reported by @Leoyzen in #46514). Config validation now rejects the combination instead of degrading silently.

**Not a duplicate:** #47934 (FP4 target on B300) and #47626 (H20 fp8) crash later, in FlashInfer draft attention; no open PR touches the draft cache-config inheritance or adds a DCP guard for dflash/dspark.

**Testing** (4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 target, RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark):
- Before: the repro from #48380 fails at draft load with the ValueError above.
- After: server boots, output coherent end-to-end; 95 tok/s N=1, 341 tok/s aggregate N=8, mean accepted length ~2.4 (metrics: 4065 accepted / 2999 drafts / 20993 draft tokens).

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] Remove redundant all_gather_interleave in ViT split_qkv
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #49061.

PaddleOCR-VL, Ernie4.5-VL, and GLM-4.1V vision attention each carried a
byte-identical helper `all_gather_interleave()` that calls
`torch.distributed.all_gather()` directly on the tensor-parallel group's raw
`device_group`, followed by a per-rank re-split, inside `split_qkv()`.

There are two problems.

First, portability. The vision encoder runs eagerly (`torch.no_grad()`, outside
`torch.compile`). On any platform whose `device_group` has no c10d backend
registered for eager use, the direct `dist.all_gather()` raises
`RuntimeError: No backend type associated with device type`, which crashes the
vision-encoder worker with `EngineDeadError` for every image request at
`tensor_parallel_size > 1`. vLLM's collective API
(`tensor_model_parallel_all_gather`, routed through `GroupCoordinator`) exists to
handle exactly this case, and the hand-rolled helper bypassed it.

Second, redundancy. The gather is a no-op. Each rank's local qkv out of
`QKVParallelLinear` (`gather_output=False`) is `[q_shard | k_shard | v_shard]`
for that rank's own heads. `all_gather_interleave` gathers every rank, reorders
to `[all_q | all_k | all_v]`, then `split_tensor_along_last_dim(...)[tp_rank]`
selects back exactly this rank's own shards. For full multi-head self-attention
(`total_num_kv_heads == total_num_heads`, which all three models use) the whole
round-trip is a numerical identity, so chunking the local tensor directly is
bit-identical.

This is the same removal already merged for `glm4_1v` in #23441
("Remove redundant all gather + split"), which fixed that model's `split_qkv`
but left the now-dead `all_gather_interleave` helper behind.

## Changes

- `paddleocr_vl.py`, `ernie45_vl.py`: drop the `all_gather_interleave` gather and
  the subsequent per-rank re-split from `split_qkv`, keeping `qkv.chunk(3, dim=2)`
  and the reshape. This matches the already-merged `glm4_1v.split_qkv`.
- All three files: delete the now-unused module-level `all_gather_interleave`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Resolve $ref/$defs in tool schemas and preserve definitions
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #46924. Supersedes #46925 (incomplete fix) and #46170 (`pop`→`get` only).

Tool schemas generated by Pydantic v2 use `$defs`/`$ref` to define nested types. Two bugs caused nested object arguments (e.g. `{"kind": "week"}`) to be double-encoded as JSON strings:

1. **No `$ref` resolution** — `find_tool_properties()` returned raw `$ref` pointers, and `extract_types_from_schema()` fell back to `["string"]` for unresolved references. This caused nested objects to be treated as strings.

2. **Destructive `pop("$defs")`** — `_get_tool_schema_defs()` used `params.pop("$defs", {})`, mutating the tool's parameter dict. On the streaming/engine path where `_get_tool_schema_defs` runs before `find_tool_properties`, the `$defs` were already gone, making ref resolution impossible even if added.

### Fix

- Add `_resolve_refs()` helper that inlines `$ref` pointers against `$defs` (Pydantic v2) and `definitions` (JSON Schema draft-07), with JSON Pointer escape decoding (`~0`→`~`, `~1`→`/`) and bounded recursion for cyclic schemas.
- Extract `_resolved_tool_properties()` to unify resolution for both definition namespaces.
- Update `find_tool_properties()` to resolve refs before returning — all downstream callers (qwen3_coder, deepseek_v32, seed_oss, glm4_moe, parser engine) automatically get concrete type information.
- Change `params.pop("$defs", {})` to `params.get("$defs", {})` in `_get_tool_schema_defs()` so definitions survive for subsequent argument coercion.

### Credit

This fix incorporates insights from:
- @hclsys who identified the `pop` ordering issue in #46925
- @alexeldeib who provided a complete supplementary patch with legacy defs support, cycle protection, and JSON Pointer decoding based on production traffic

# New defs-preservation tests

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A streaming tool call can end with `finish_reason` set while `arguments` is cut off mid-string. Any client that calls `json.loads` on the accumulated arguments fails on it. Reproduced live on Qwen3.8-27B in 7 of 25 requests sent straight at the worker, no proxy in the path.

`_safe_arg_prefix` (`parser_engine.py:283`) deliberately streams unterminated string values for prefix-stable keys. Its own docstring carries the contract: "String values for keys in `string_keys` are prefix-stable, so stream their unterminated content instead of buffering long arguments until the closing tag arrives." Something has to close them, and that something is the flush.

`_flush_arg_converter` (`parser_engine.py:963`) re-derives the arguments with `partial=False`. Every in-tree `arg_converter` builds its result from completed parameters and folds the still-open one in under `if partial:`. So when generation ends while a parameter is open, the non-partial re-derivation **drops that parameter**, and the result is neither longer than nor a prefix of what was already streamed. Both guards fail, the function returns `None`, and nothing ever terminates the prefix the client is holding.

This is not conditional on the model misbehaving. Anything that ends generation with a parameter open reaches it: a `max_tokens` stop, a stop string, or a malformed continuation.

Fuse the clamped MoE activation path into FP8 block-128 activation quantization:

1. finite SwiGLU clamping;
2. BF16 SiLU and gated multiplication;
3. dynamic E4M3 block quantization, including Hopper DeepGEMM UE8M0 scales; and

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add invalidate_merged_conv_weight() / invalidate_kda_conv_weight_caches() methods to manually clear the stale cache
- invoke invalidation before every load_weights() call so refits always rebuild from fresh weights
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache
- invoke cache invalidation before GLM-5.3 weight loading so the next access rebuilds from fresh weights

items.title: [Feature] Restore concurrent partial prefill limit (max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
items.bodyExcerpt:
Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413.

As detailed in #57413, without a cap on concurrent partial prefills, long-context RAG workloads (e.g. 100k+ tokens) completely stall V1's scheduling queue. Short requests are forced to wait for many iterations until massive partial prefills finish.

This reintroduces `max_concurrent_prefills` directly into the V1 scheduler's `WAITING` loop. By bounding how many requests can simultaneously hold partial prefill state, we allow interleaving and dramatically reduce tail TTFT (as validated by the community on 4x B200 / GLM-5.3-Flash).

pulls only the indexer-selected rows back just in time, so long-context agentic

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

## Reachability

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,
   so it is the **default** backend on GLM-4V-family servers — a plain
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
   `"media_io_kwargs": {"video": {"fps": 100000}}` is enough, no override needed.
2. It registers with the default `requires_gpu=False`, so
   `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:60`) does **not**
   strip a request-level `video_backend: "opencv_dynamic"` either. The remaining
   `merge_kwargs` handling forwards `fps` verbatim.
3. It is also selected explicitly at

Only the `duration <= max_duration` branch is exposed. The `else` branch

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Fit kpool top-k indices to AITER with a single Triton kernel
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The existing kernel is implemented in pytorch and leads to **18** elementwise kernel launched per forward. We replace it with a single triton kernel.

**Perf: -5% ITL, +3-5% out tok/s**

## What it does

GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer selects `topk + kpool_tail` tokens, where the tail size is <kpool=4 and depends on the number of tokens in the request. AITER expects a fixed topk value independent of request length. Hence we use `fit_kpool_indices_to_aiter` to select the a fixed topk tokens from history and tail respectively, and disregard any extras. 

The kernel prioritizes selecting the tokens from the tail, and then selects the highest prio tokens from the history, until topk tokens are chosen.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel` (the configuration that turns on `use_sequence_parallel_moe`) sporadically emits a wrong first token, stray `</think>` tokens followed by a repeated reasoning block, and occasionally byte garbage such as `ԥԥԥԥ� Canadian French, ԥԥ�1ԥ…`. DP with TP=1 and TP-only serving are clean.

`Glm5NextModel` follows the DeepSeek-V4 sequence-parallel layout: the token dimension is sharded across the TP group once at the model entry (`sp_shard`) and every layer runs its mHC and MLP on that shard, gathering only for attention. Every non-MoE module on the shard therefore has to be sequence-parallel aware. The dense MLP of the first `first_k_dense_replace` (3) layers was still constructed as a standard TP MLP, so its `down_proj` all-reduce summed the partial outputs of *different* tokens held by the two TP ranks:

- multi-token batches (prefill, concurrent decode): rows of the first three layers are mixed pairwise, hence the wrong first token / garbage under load;
- single-token decode: the peer rank holds a zero padding row, so the real token only loses half of the intermediate dimension, which is why the model still looked mostly coherent and the bug went unnoticed.

The shared experts already pass `is_sequence_parallel` (replicated weights, `disable_tp`, no collective). This PR passes the same flag to the dense `Glm5NextMLP` and adds a unit test for the layout. TP-only and DP-with-TP1 deployments do not enter this branch and are unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix] Pin num_splits for the FA4 hd256 kernel in sparse MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`SparseMLAAttention._run_masked_mha` calls `flash_attn_varlen_func` with `fa_version=4` but never pins `num_splits`. On Blackwell (SM100/SM110) with `head_size == head_size_v == 256`, FA4 dispatches its dedicated hd256 kernel, which asserts `not is_split_kv`. Once the batch is large enough for the split-KV heuristic to fire, that assertion trips and takes down the engine core.

This affects `glm_moe_dsa` models (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 family), whose `v_head_dim` is 256.

## Symptom

```
assert not is_split_kv, "SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support SplitKV"
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed / engine core proc died
```

Reproduced on 4x B200 (TP=4), `max_model_len 32768`, GLM-5.2 NVFP4: serving is stable at low load and the engine dies once concurrency reaches roughly 32. Below that threshold the heuristic does not split, which is why this does not show up in small smoke tests.

## Root cause

The dense FA path already knows this kernel cannot split — `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel` exists in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py` and is consulted in `flash_attn.py`. The sparse MLA call site is the one place that builds FA4 kwargs for the same kernel without the corresponding guard.

## Fix

Pin `num_splits = 1` when the hd256 kernel is in play, reusing the existing helper rather than hardcoding the head size:

```python
if uses_fa4_hd256_kernel(q.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]):
    kwargs["num_splits"] = 1
```

The helper already checks the device capability (major in `(10, 11)`), so this is a no-op on every other platform and on every other head size. No behaviour change outside the configuration that currently crashes.

## Test

Verified on `v0.29.0` with the equivalent guard applied to the same call site: the engine survives a concurrency sweep of 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 with zero failed requests, where the unpatched build dies at 32. The change in this PR is rebased onto `main` and switched to the existing helper; I do not have a Blackwell box

items.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM90 sparse MLA IMA on >16k-row steps by chunking plan/run
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a CUDA illegal-memory-access crash whenever a single scheduled step packs more than 16384 query rows on the SM90 sparse MLA backend (the GLM-5.3-Flash default), e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` with a 28k-token prefill chunk, or 32k tokens scheduled across concurrent requests.

**Root cause (flashinfer 0.6.18.post1, the pinned version).** The SM90 batch-MLA plan hardcodes `max_total_num_works = 16384` and never checks it: the load-balancing schedule is `std::copy`'d into per-array regions sized for 16384 works, so a larger step silently overwrites neighboring schedule arrays, and the kernel then reads garbage `q_indptr`/`kv_indptr` (IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`). This backend feeds one varlen row per query token, so any step with more than 16384 scheduled tokens overflows. flashinfer 0.7.0 raised the limit to 65536 and added a hard error, but vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`. Small overflows (e.g. 16385 works) do not even fault — they run with a corrupted schedule.

**Fix.** When a step has more than `_MAX_PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS = 8192` query rows, plan and run the MQA as independent row chunks: the builder plans each chunk into its own `_SM90State` (a lazily grown pool), and `forward_mqa` runs each state's row range and concatenates. Each row is already an independent varlen query (causality is encoded in the top-k selection, `causal=False`), so chunking is exact. The bound is 8192 rather than 16384 so the work count stays provably under 16384 even with split-kv rows: works <= rows + total_kv_len / kv_len_limit, and `kv_len_limit` tracks total_kv_len / num_clusters. Steps at or under the limit keep the existing single-plan path unchanged, including CUDA-graph replay.

## Not a duplicate

- #56969 fixed a different OOB in this backend (mixed prefill/decode batches); it is in the tested tree and the crash still reproduces without this change.
- #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and the indexer prefill workspace sizing; different call sites.
